concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor conceded that no admissible evidence shows the final launch model card or certification record contains the required explicit disclosure. That is a reframing of the existing gap, not new evidence closing it.
The Actor conceded that no approved risk acceptance is in evidence and did not provide any signed approval covering outage-response exposure. The unsigned draft remains insufficient under policy.

The Actor accepted that rollout controls alone are insufficient and did not provide evidence that the outage-response segment was excluded from the rollout cohort. The exposure condition remains unresolved.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence. The response materially narrows the claim and correctly abandons the unsupported controls-alone theory, but that is reinterpretation of the same record, not evidence of compliance. The admissible evidence still shows: the outage-response segment is below target and remains exposed in rollout; policy requires disclosure unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance; the available risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not address the exposed segment; and no final model card or certification artifact is in evidence showing the required disclosure was actually made. Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal support operational readiness, but they do not satisfy the disclosure predicate. Because the missing compliance predicate remains unresolved, a move to compliant_with_caveats is not supported on this record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the final model card or certification record actually discloses the outage-response limitation before launch.
No approved risk acceptance is in evidence for continued exposure of the weak outage segment.
The rollout controls do not exclude the affected outage-response use case from exposure, and policy says those controls do not remove disclosure duties when the segment remains exposed.
